title: Add SAML SSO support for Enterprise customers
body:
## Problem

We currently support email/password and Google OAuth for all tiers, but Enterprise customers consistently ask for SAML 2.0 SSO so their existing IdP (Okta, OneLogin, Azure AD) can manage access centrally.

## Proposal

Add a SAML 2.0 SSO option for the Enterprise tier:

- Admin can configure SAML metadata (URL or XML upload)
- Just-in-time user provisioning on first login
- Group-based role mapping from IdP attributes
- Forced SSO mode (workspace admin can disable email/password for the workspace)
- Audit log entries for SSO config changes and SSO sessions

## Why now

Deals lost in the last quarter cited 'no SAML' as a top-3 blocker. Three current Enterprise prospects ($1.4M ARR combined) have made it a contract requirement.

## Scope

In scope:
- SAML 2.0 only (not OIDC for Enterprise — that's separate)
- Okta, OneLogin, Azure AD tested as primary IdPs
- Self-serve admin UI for SAML config

Out of scope:
- SCIM provisioning (separate issue #4291)
- Multi-IdP per workspace (only one SAML config per workspace)
- Service Provider initiated SSO from custom domains (just IdP-initiated for now)

## Existing constraints

Our auth middleware currently assumes a single OIDC identity per user (after the Google SSO work in #3801). SAML adds a second IdP class — we'll need to extend the identity model again, or enforce a 'one SSO type per workspace' rule in admin UI.

The audit log schema added in #4112 covers user-action events but not workspace-config-change events; we'll need to extend it.

## Compliance

This is a SOC2-relevant change. Audit log parity with email/password sessions is a hard requirement (mentioned in our Type II report).

## Timing

Q4 sales kickoff is Oct 28. Sales would like a GA-or-late-beta announcement by then.
